messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

substance.description: The substance for which to calculate the boiling point.

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) the melting/freezing point of pure water drops below the normal 0 °C.  
Using the ice–water phase‑diagram (or the Clausius–Clapeyron relation for the solid–liquid transition), the equilibrium temperature at 10 kPa is approximately:

**≈ –2 °C**

So water would freeze at about –2 °C when the ambient pressure is 10 kPa.
